scope: Independent new retrieval safety unit/HTTP cases. Existing passing curriculum tests and prior UI groups were not repeated. Seven groups passed together after six previously failing regressions were fixed and one actual-asthma resemblance case was newly added; the eighth new follow-up-after-abstention case passed separately after its guard was implemented.

results.name: unknown clinical topic names cannot bypass evidence requirements through conversational wording
a follow-up must not jump backward across a newer unsupported clinical topic
quantitative medication requests expressed without the word dose require dose evidence
ambiguous clinical acronyms in a study-habit request do not confer condition coverage
unlinked unknown-topic chat abstains without dispatching a provider request
generic follow-up follows the latest named topic rather than the original linked-condition anchor
an actual asthma record does not grant coverage for an asthma-like resemblance term
a generic follow-up after an unsupported answer cannot reactivate an old topic through shared vocabulary

findingsFixed: Unknown clinical names phrased conversationally could previously reach unrestricted generic inference. Unmatched queries now require evidence except narrow nonclinical coaching intent.

Generic follow-up could previously skip a newer unknown topic and reuse older evidence, or revert to the original linked condition after a named topic switch. Latest topic continuity and grounded single-condition anchors now take precedence.
Medication quantity synonyms could previously bypass the dose evidence guard. Quantity/strength/puff/infusion requests are included.
SMART and CAP in nonclinical study-habit requests could previously confer clinical condition coverage. Nonclinical intent now suppresses retrieval.
A condition-like resemblance token could previously be treated as a named diagnosis. Actual Asthma fixture is now tested, rather than unrelated COPD-only fixtures.
A generic follow-up after an unsupported answer could reactivate an old topic through shared vocabulary. It now abstains without another provider request.
remainingLimitations: The selector can choose only canonical snippets or original questions, reducing fabricated body/citation risk. This does not establish that every summary or keyed answer is medically correct.
Official-source reading, actual corpus condition counts, freshness and medical editorial validation remain separate source/content checks.
All teaching content remains pending clinician review.
